abstract:
We study the stationary law of the fair Collatz affine maps acting jointly on the real and ternary coordinates. Leen's counted-coalescence estimate yields sharp inverse-square-root decay of bounded seed-image volumes. Same-count geometry gives matching density moments, half-logarithmic conditional coding entropy, and bounded information in the odd count. A stationary integer partition identifies coding multiplicity with class size; Fourier Wren's independent posterior formulation sharpens the seed-length dependence. The accelerated clock has analogous bounds.

The joint law is purely singular but exact dimensional of full product dimension two. Its smoothed densities have sharp logarithmic moment and entropy growth, and two-point ball probabilities have order $r^2\sqrt{\log(1/r)}$. The unit-seed image union captures stationary probability $1-O(n^{-1/2})$.

On the compact quotient by the diagonal $\mathbb Z[1/3]$, dyadic pushforwards converge weakly to Haar measure although each remains singular. An exact binomial identity turns multiplication by two into an average of powers of three. A digit-window entropy argument gives finite-partition relative entropy at depth $k$ at most $Ck\log(n+2)/\sqrt{n+1}$ and Wasserstein distance at most $C\sqrt{\log(n+2)}(n+1)^{-1/4}$. The concentration bound also implies almost-sure normality of the real coordinate in every integer base.

Leen's orbit-set sparsity separates nonperiodic integer codes from the real endpoint; simultaneous integer values occur precisely on inverse-cycle codes. The law nevertheless has full support. Using Valbuena's trace and the previously constructed inverse law, we identify canonical Cesaro real fibres at specified odd integers. Nonperiodic fibres retain a relative gap; periodic fibres have linear endpoint mass and no endpoint atom. These geometric results supply no uniform moving-integer estimate and do not establish universal Collatz convergence.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds a complete metric theorem: the singular joint law has exact dimension two, sharp logarithmic smoothing moments, half-log-log smoothing entropy, two-point small-ball probability of order r^2 sqrt(log(1/r)), and near-critical energy of order (2-s)^(-3/2). The proof uses exponential coupling for upper bounds, controlled neighborhoods of exact image unions for lower bounds, and a dyadic conditional mixture that retains the full stationary tail in the entropy estimate. Also proves that the unit-seed image union captures stationary probability 1-O(n^(-1/2)), and that a uniform seed interval of length L loses at most C(1+log L)/sqrt(n+1) probability outside that union; this is explicitly distinguished from Haar-volume comparison and integer-diagonal behavior. Addresses the version-1 review by explicitly realizing each random word from an independent Haar binary seed in Sections 6 and 8.2, quoting the pair-absorption tail in its source form, stating null-boundary conventions, and emphasizing that the common even coast precedes accelerated extension. Also determines the full support and closure of the finite-real code image as [0,infinity) times the ternary units, and proves a uniform lower ball bound with exponent 7.248619... on every compact positive real interval, without a synchronization or sparsity input. A fourth bounded exact audit checks the constructive real and integer inverse interfaces; the three earlier audits remain unchanged. No numerical extrapolation is an input to any analytic result. Adds a canonical real-fibre theorem at each specified positive odd unit: the Cesaro average of the 3^k-normalized joint ternary-cylinder slices converges weakly to the known integer trace times the real pushforward of the known inverse Markov law. The proof retains one terminal ternary digit, controls the stationary real tail by a fractional moment, and applies the prior bounded selection identity. A geometric cycle renewal gives endpoint probability comparable to epsilon/a at periodic roots, with no endpoint atom; nonperiodic fibres retain the uniform relative gap. Existing path-law and correction-distribution results are explicitly credited. No individual-depth convergence or root-uniform rate is claimed. The four exact audit programs and their results are unchanged. Adds a compact-quotient theorem: dyadic pushforwards of the projected joint law converge weakly to Haar while all finite-stage laws remain singular. The exact identity D2_*mu=(mu+D3_*mu)/2 gives a binomial mixture; near-maximal finite digit entropy and an exact consecutive-digit recoding prove partition KL at depth k at most C*k*log(n+2)/sqrt(n+1). A multiscale approximation gives Wasserstein distance at most C*sqrt(log(n+2))*(n+1)^(-1/4). The proof keeps quotient maps, boundaries, all entropy terms, and conditioning losses explicit. A standard normality corollary for the real random coordinate follows from the previously proved concentration bound. Related times-two/times-three invariant-measure results are cited as context, not imported inputs. A fifth frozen exact audit verifies 180 finite-law comparisons, 70080 direct point evaluations, and 16440 digit identities. The first four audits are unchanged. No claim about an individual integer orbit follows from the quotient limit.
title: Geometry, integer fibres, and dyadic equidistribution of the joint Collatz affine law
